title: The Third Order
hook: laypeople who follow Francis in family and work

segments.voice: Yesterday, the Poor Clares: enclosed, poor, glad, praying for a world that rarely sees them. Your line was hidden prayer. What did you do that nobody knew about? Day one thousand two hundred sixteen.

A preacher has just finished, and the whole town wants to go with him. That's the scene in the Little Flowers, in a village near Assisi called Cannara, the same chapter that tells of the birds. Francis preaches, and the people are so moved that men and women alike want to leave their houses, their fields, their families, and follow him on the road. On paper, a preacher's dream: a whole village signing up. But Francis says no. Don't be in a hurry, he tells them. Don't leave. I'll arrange what you should do. So there are first the brothers, and second Clare's sisters. What do you do with everyone else? Today, the answer.
screen: `A WHOLE TOWN WANTS TO FOLLOW.` → `DON'T BE IN A HURRY.` → `WHAT ABOUT EVERYONE ELSE?`

segments.voice: The Little Flowers says that after Cannara, Francis began to think about a third order, for people who would follow him without leaving home. Married people. Parents. Farmers, merchants, workers. In the early days they were called the brothers and sisters of penance, and penance there doesn't mean misery. It means turning, a whole life turned toward God. Today the Church calls it the Secular Franciscan Order, secular meaning lived in the world, not in a cloister. Francis wrote a letter to people like this, to all the faithful living in the world. In it he says, more or less: love God with your whole heart, love your neighbor as yourself, turn from what pulls you away, receive the Body and Blood of the Lord. And then he says something startling. People who live like that, he writes, are the spouses and brothers and mothers of Jesus Christ. He's leaning on the gospel, where Jesus says, in the Douay-Rheims: "whosoever shall do the will of my Father, that is in heaven, he is my brother, and my sister, and my mother." Not a monk. Not a friar. Anyone. That's what the Third Order is built on. You don't need a habit or a monastery to belong to Francis's family. The poverty looks different at home. It might be a simpler house, a lighter grip on things, generosity with time. The peace looks different: a kitchen table, an office, a difficult relative. Secular Franciscans make a promise, meet in local groups, and go back to their lives. The point was never to run away from ordinary life. The point was to bring Francis into it.
screen: `A THIRD WAY: FOLLOW WITHOUT LEAVING.` · `PENANCE MEANS TURNING.` · `BROTHER, SISTER AND MOTHER OF CHRIST.` · `POVERTY AND PEACE AT THE KITCHEN TABLE.` · then, large: `HE IS MY BROTHER, AND MY SISTER, AND MY MOTHER.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: choose one Franciscan habit for today. Settle, and breathe. Look back over this week's stories. Patience at a closed gate. Asking what the wolf is hungry for. Stopping for a bird. A good thing done in secret. Let one of them choose you. Then put it somewhere specific in your ordinary day: the commute, the dishes, the meeting, the call with your mother. See yourself doing it there. If you pray, you can ask Francis's God for help to keep it. If you don't, just hold the picture steady, and breathe. The bell holds the time.
Third Order. Laypeople who follow Francis without leaving home, living his gospel in family and work. Today's word.
Your line: francis at home. Today, do your one Franciscan habit somewhere completely ordinary, and notice whether the place changes. Day one thousand two hundred sixteen.

howItsDone: Secular Franciscans are lay Catholics, single or married, who make a profession to live the gospel in the spirit of Francis, meet regularly in local fraternities, and carry that life into their families and work.

original.note: Latin: penance, a change of heart; the early name of the Third Order was the order of penance.

trapdoor: what you thought: an order is for monks and nuns.
what it means: a third way for laypeople, married or single, to follow Francis at home and at work.
what a scholar hears: Francis's letter to the faithful calls such people spouses, brothers and mothers of Christ, echoing Matthew 12:50.
